attribution.note: Marcus's own annotation in his own post, replying to Hinton's quoted line.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the 'a lot of us still think' framing. It is a checkable claim that a body of skeptics exists, not a claim that Hinton is wrong.

contract.note: The plain reading, a recognisable body of researchers beyond Marcus with no majority implied, is an ordinary reading of 'a lot of us'. Using 2023 up to publication as the window is reasonable.

evidence.note: Mitchell and Krakauer (Feb 2023) describe a stark debate in the field and say LLMs remain brittle. Independent researchers, inside the target period.
Six researchers (Jan 2023) argue that LLMs fail at functional competence and are incomplete models of thought. Independent group, inside the target period.

reviews.rationale: Two independent 2023 papers by eight researchers in total publicly hold that understanding and reasoning remained unsolved. That meets the support condition of multiple independent researchers holding a substantial position. Nothing in the packet shows the view was confined to Marcus or a fringe. The packet does not show that these researchers commented on the interview itself, but the contract does not require that.

attribution.note: Marcus's own annotation, framed as sharp disagreement with Hinton.

semantics.note: 'I don't think', paired with 'sharply disagree', is a firm opinion, not a hedge. The proposition keeps the scope (flexible novel reasoning, in a reliable way). Marcus's caveat that the issue is 'partly definitional' is left out.

contract.note: Reading 'reliable' as dependable transfer is fair. The result depends on an operational meaning of 'understand' that Marcus did not supply, and the July–September 2023 window is inferred.

evidence.note: The Reversal Curse (posted 21 Sep 2023) shows a deduction failure that holds across model families, including GPT-4. This partly supports the reliability component only. It says nothing about understanding.
GPT-3 matched humans on zero-shot digit matrices. This predates the target quarter and is a single success, so it is context, not a contradiction.

reviews.rationale: The support condition has two parts: recurring transfer failures across systems, and a defensible account linking them to understanding. e3 gives one robust failure type, which partly supports the reliability component. Nothing in the packet operationalises 'understand'. e4 is an earlier, isolated success. The packet does not settle the claim either way.

attribution.note: Marcus's own annotation replying to Hinton on drug design.

semantics.note: 'As far as I know' limits the claim to Marcus's knowledge; it does not express a probability, so the claim can still be checked against the record. The proposition keeps that qualifier.

contract.note: In context the claim is about drug design, so reading it as AI-designed molecules is fair. Under a broader reading that includes repurposing, baricitinib could count against him. The efficacy threshold is the drafter's choice.

evidence.note: Insilico's own disclosure (Jun 2023): its AI-designed drug INS018_055 had only safety data and was just entering Phase II. It is still a candidate, but this covers one molecule only.
BenevolentAI's own disclosure (Apr 2023): BEN-2293 missed its efficacy endpoints, with only an exploratory subgroup signal. One molecule only.
Baricitinib was an existing drug repurposed with AI help and shown to work clinically. Under the drug-design reading it does not qualify, but it would contradict a broader reading.

reviews.rationale: Two company disclosures confirm that two AI-designed molecules had not shown efficacy. Support, though, requires a reasonably complete account of all AI-designed clinical candidates, and the packet admits it has none. No AI-designed drug with proven efficacy appears in the packet, so nothing contradicts the claim either. The universal negative is not established.

attribution.note: The 'Zero' line is Marcus's own. The 2016 line he quotes is Hinton's and serves only as background.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the exact count of zero and the seven-year window from 2016 to 2023.

contract.note: Reading 'zero' globally and as whole jobs is strict, but Marcus chose an exact number. Defining 'replaced' as a job eliminated, not a task automated, is fair. Under this contract support is nearly impossible to establish.

evidence.note: The 2022 UK census shows workforce growth and shortages. It covers the UK only and is a net count, so it does not measure displacement caused by machines.
Oxipit announced its autonomous chest X-ray system in Mar 2022. This is a company disclosure about capability and does not document any radiologist losing a job.

reviews.rationale: The packet documents no radiologist whose job was eliminated by a machine, so the contradiction condition is not met. It also has no complete global record showing zero such cases, so the support condition is not met either. UK workforce growth and one product announcement are context only.
